title: The Qur'an says its message is 'for whoever has a heart.' But doesn't everyone?

beats.narration: The Qur'an says its message is 'for whoever has a heart.' But doesn't everyone already have one?
The verse offers its reminder 'for whoever has a heart' — *qalb*. Which is strange, since everyone has one. So notice what it isn't saying: it isn't talking about the organ beating in your chest.

Here's where it gets interesting: elsewhere the Qur'an says it is not the eyes that go blind, but the hearts — the ones inside the chest. A heart, here, means the capacity to actually take something in.

verse.highlight_phrase_en: but the hearts that go blind

beats.narration: So 'whoever has a heart' isn't everyone — it's whoever keeps that capacity awake. The reminder is offered to all, but it only lands where a heart is still open enough to receive it.
